explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to lower the shutter', this idiom is the standard way in Spain to describe a business closing, either for the day or permanently. It provides a more vivid, physical image than the simple verb 'cerrar'. It is widely used in both everyday speech and economic journalism.

examples.en_text: The neighborhood bakery has closed down after thirty years of service.
examples.target_text: La panadería del barrio ha bajado la persiana después de treinta años de servicio.

examples.en_text: It was already very late, so they pulled down the shutters and went to sleep.
examples.target_text: Ya era muy tarde, así que bajaron las persianas y se fueron a dormir.

examples.en_text: If sales don't improve this month, many shops will have to close down.
examples.target_text: Si las ventas no mejoran este mes, muchas tiendas tendrán que bajar la persiana.

examples.en_text: When the sun shines directly on the window, I pull down the shutter to keep the house cool.
examples.target_text: Cuando el sol da directamente en la ventana, bajo la persiana para mantener la casa fresca.

examples.en_text: The bookstore on the corner closed down last week because they couldn't pay the rent.
examples.target_text: La librería de la esquina bajó la persiana la semana pasada porque no podía pagar el alquiler.

examples.en_text: Several travel agencies in the area have closed down due to a lack of customers.
examples.target_text: Varias agencias de viajes de la zona han bajado la persiana por falta de clientes.

explanation_en: This verb construction means 'to brand as', 'to label as', or 'to accuse of being' (usually something negative). It requires the preposition 'de' before the adjective or noun that represents the accusation. It is a staple of political discourse and journalistic Spanish to describe criticism.

examples.en_text: The press always brands him as a liar, but he insists he is telling the truth.
examples.target_text: La prensa siempre lo tacha de mentiroso, pero él insiste en que dice la verdad.

examples.en_text: Many criticized the director and labeled him as incompetent after the project's failure.
examples.target_text: Muchos criticaron al director y lo tacharon de incompetente tras el fracaso del proyecto.

examples.en_text: You cannot label everyone who disagrees with you as selfish.
examples.target_text: No puedes tachar a todo el que no esté de acuerdo contigo de egoísta.

examples.en_text: Some neighbors have branded her as irresponsible for leaving her pets alone.
examples.target_text: Algunos vecinos la han tachado de irresponsable por dejar a sus mascotas solas.

examples.en_text: If you say what you really think in that meeting, they will label you as a rebel.
examples.target_text: Si dices lo que realmente piensas en esa reunión, te tacharán de rebelde.

examples.en_text: It is unfair to brand today's youth as lazy.
examples.target_text: Es injusto tachar de perezosos a los jóvenes de hoy en día.

idiom: para el común de los mortales
explanation_en: This expression literally translates to 'for the common of mortals' and is used to refer to ordinary people as opposed to specialists, elites, or those with inside knowledge. It carries a slightly elevated or humorous tone and is very common in journalistic writing and everyday conversations when discussing complex topics.

examples.en_text: Buying a house in the city center is an impossible dream for the average person.
examples.target_text: Comprar una casa en el centro de la ciudad es un sueño imposible para el común de los mortales.

examples.en_text: This new smartphone has too many useless features for the average person.
examples.target_text: Este nuevo teléfono inteligente tiene demasiadas funciones inútiles para el común de los mortales.

examples.en_text: Abstract art is sometimes very difficult to understand for ordinary mortals.
examples.target_text: El arte abstracto a veces resulta muy difícil de entender para el común de los mortales.

examples.en_text: Traveling in first class is a luxury that is not available to the average person.
examples.target_text: Viajar en primera clase es un lujo que no está disponible para el común de los mortales.

examples.en_text: Filling out these tax forms is too complicated for the average person.
examples.target_text: Rellenar estos formularios de impuestos es demasiado complicado para el común de los mortales.

examples.en_text: Working fifteen hours a day is neither healthy nor sustainable for the average person.
examples.target_text: Trabajar quince horas al día no es algo saludable ni sostenible para el común de los mortales.

explanation_en: This colloquial but widely accepted idiom combines the verb 'pillar' (to catch/grab) with 'desprevenido' (unprepared). It is the standard way in Spain to say someone was caught by surprise. In Latin America, 'tomar desprevenido' or 'agarrar desprevenido' are often preferred.

examples.en_text: The surprise math exam caught us completely off guard.
examples.target_text: El examen sorpresa de matemáticas nos pilló totalmente desprevenidos.

examples.en_text: His question about my professional future caught me off guard.
examples.target_text: Su pregunta sobre mi futuro laboral me pilló desprevenido.

examples.en_text: The storm caught us off guard and we didn't have umbrellas.
examples.target_text: La tormenta nos pilló desprevenidos y no llevábamos paraguas.

examples.en_text: The announcement of the company's closure caught the employees off guard.
examples.target_text: El anuncio del cierre de la empresa pilló desprevenidos a los empleados.

examples.en_text: When he proposed to me, it caught me completely off guard.
examples.target_text: Cuando me pidió matrimonio, me pilló completamente desprevenida.

examples.en_text: The goal in the first minute of the game caught the rival team off guard.
examples.target_text: El gol en el primer minuto de juego pilló desprevenido al equipo rival.

explanation_en: This fixed collocation means to confront or deal with a difficult situation, problem, or financial obligation. It is a more natural and sophisticated alternative to 'enfrentar' or 'responder a' in professional and everyday Spanish.

examples.en_text: We have to face the new expenses of this month.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que hacer frente a los nuevos gastos de este mes.

examples.en_text: She faced her fears and spoke in public.
examples.target_text: Ella hizo frente a sus miedos y habló en público.

examples.en_text: The company doesn't know how to deal with the current crisis.
examples.target_text: La empresa no sabe cómo hacer frente a la crisis actual.

examples.en_text: The citizens will face the water problem together.
examples.target_text: Los ciudadanos harán frente al problema del agua juntos.

examples.en_text: If you don't confront your problems now, they will be worse in the future.
examples.target_text: Si no haces frente a tus problemas ahora, serán peores en el futuro.

examples.en_text: It is necessary for the government to address the inflation immediately.
examples.target_text: Es necesario que el gobierno haga frente a la inflación de inmediato.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to arm-wrestle,' this idiom is widely used metaphorically in politics, business, and daily life to describe a power struggle or a test of wills between two opposing forces. It implies a tense situation where neither side wants to back down.

examples.en_text: I don't think it's a good idea to engage in this trial of strength with the director; you could lose your job.
examples.target_text: No creo que sea una buena idea echarle este pulso al director; podrías perder tu empleo.

examples.en_text: The union decided to engage in this trial of strength with the government to get better salaries.
examples.target_text: El sindicato decidió echar este pulso al gobierno para conseguir mejores salarios.

examples.en_text: As a parent, sometimes you have to engage in this trial of strength with your children so they learn the rules.
examples.target_text: Como padre, a veces tienes que echarles este pulso a tus hijos para que aprendan las normas.

examples.en_text: Our company is willing to engage in this trial of strength with the competition to dominate the market.
examples.target_text: Nuestra empresa está dispuesta a echar este pulso a la competencia para dominar el mercado.

examples.en_text: I know it's risky, but I'm going to engage in this trial of strength with my boss because I deserve a raise.
examples.target_text: Sé que es arriesgado, pero le voy a echar este pulso a mi jefe porque merezco un aumento.

examples.en_text: The neighbors united to engage in this trial of strength with the construction company that wanted to destroy the park.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos se unieron para echar este pulso a la constructora que quería destruir el parque.

explanation_en: A very common idiomatic adverbial phrase meaning 'as quickly as possible' or 'without delay.' It is more common and natural in spoken and written Spanish than 'lo antes posible.' It can be used in both formal and informal contexts.

examples.en_text: Please send me the report as soon as possible so I can review it.
examples.target_text: Por favor, envíame el informe cuanto antes para que pueda revisarlo.

examples.en_text: You have a very bad cough, you should go to the doctor as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: Tienes una tos muy fea, deberías ir al médico cuanto antes.

examples.en_text: If we want to get cheap flights, we have to book them as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: Si queremos conseguir vuelos baratos, tenemos que reservarlos cuanto antes.

examples.en_text: I am sorry for the misunderstanding; we will try to solve this problem as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: Lamento el malentendido; intentaremos solucionar este problema cuanto antes.

examples.en_text: We haven't seen each other in a long time, we have to have a coffee as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: Hace mucho tiempo que no nos vemos, tenemos que tomar un café cuanto antes.

examples.en_text: The director needs an answer, so we must make a decision as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: El director necesita una respuesta, así que debemos tomar una decisión cuanto antes.

explanation_en: A very common journalistic and political idiom meaning to highlight, emphasize, or showcase the worth or importance of something. It is often used in professional, political, and cultural contexts to discuss assets, efforts, or policies.

examples.en_text: The new museum highlights the history and traditions of the town.
examples.target_text: El nuevo museo pone en valor la historia y las tradiciones del pueblo.

examples.en_text: On your resume, you must showcase your experience working in a team.
examples.target_text: En tu currículum debes poner en valor tu experiencia trabajando en equipo.

examples.en_text: This initiative highlights the region's organic products.
examples.target_text: Esta iniciativa pone en valor los productos ecológicos de la región.

examples.en_text: The teacher always values the effort of her students more than the grades.
examples.target_text: La profesora siempre pone en valor el esfuerzo de sus alumnos más que las notas.

examples.en_text: The renovation of the building showcased the original stone walls.
examples.target_text: La reforma del edificio puso en valor las paredes de piedra originales.

examples.en_text: We want to do an advertising campaign that highlights our customer service.
examples.target_text: Queremos hacer una campaña de publicidad que ponga en valor nuestro servicio al cliente.

idiom: de la noche a la mañana
explanation_en: This idiom is used to describe a sudden, unexpected change that happens very quickly, literally 'from night to morning.' It is extremely common in both spoken and written Spanish across all registers. It is often used to emphasize the dramatic nature of a sudden shift in circumstances.

examples.en_text: You can't expect to get rich overnight; everything requires effort.
examples.target_text: No puedes esperar hacerte rico de la noche a la mañana; todo requiere esfuerzo.

examples.en_text: She decided to quit her job overnight to travel the world.
examples.target_text: Decidió dejar su trabajo de la noche a la mañana para viajar por el mundo.

examples.en_text: The weather changed overnight and it started to get very cold.
examples.target_text: El clima cambió de la noche a la mañana y empezó a hacer mucho frío.

examples.en_text: The young singer became famous overnight thanks to social media.
examples.target_text: El joven cantante se volvió famoso de la noche a la mañana gracias a las redes sociales.

examples.en_text: His attitude toward me changed overnight and I don't understand why.
examples.target_text: Su actitud hacia mí cambió de la noche a la mañana y no entiendo por qué.

examples.en_text: You are not going to learn to speak Spanish overnight; you need patience.
examples.target_text: No vas a aprender a hablar español de la noche a la mañana, necesitas paciencia.

explanation_en: In journalism, 'última hora' refers to breaking news or the latest developments of an ongoing event. In everyday speech, 'a última hora' means 'at the last minute.' It is a highly frequent collocation in both contexts.

examples.en_text: We interrupt our programming to bring you breaking news about the accident downtown.
examples.target_text: Interrumpimos la programación para darles una noticia de última hora sobre el accidente en el centro.

examples.en_text: Have you heard the latest update on the presidential elections?
examples.target_text: ¿Has escuchado la última hora sobre las elecciones presidenciales?

examples.en_text: The director asked us for a report with the latest updates on the project before the meeting.
examples.target_text: El director nos pidió un informe con la última hora del proyecto antes de la reunión.

examples.en_text: According to the latest updates, the star player has decided to stay with the team.
examples.target_text: Según la información de última hora, el jugador estrella ha decidido quedarse en el equipo.

examples.en_text: The radio is broadcasting the latest updates on the storm approaching the coast.
examples.target_text: La radio está transmitiendo la última hora sobre la tormenta que se acerca a la costa.

examples.en_text: We want to know the latest developments in the peace negotiations between both countries.
examples.target_text: Queremos conocer la última hora de las negociaciones de paz entre ambos países.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression means to have a grudge against someone, to be eager to confront them, or to want to get back at them. Depending on the context, it can also mean to look forward to something or even have sexual desire, but in political and everyday conflict contexts, it denotes a desire to defeat or punish someone.

examples.en_text: Since Juan reported the mistake, his office coworkers have it in for him.
examples.target_text: Desde que Juan reportó el error, sus compañeros de oficina le tienen ganas.

examples.en_text: Tomorrow I play against the tournament champion; I've been eager to face him since last year.
examples.target_text: Mañana juego contra el campeón del torneo; le tengo ganas desde el año pasado.

examples.en_text: Be careful with the boss, it's obvious he has it in for your coworker because of what he said in the meeting.
examples.target_text: Ten cuidado con el jefe, se nota que le tiene ganas a tu compañero por lo que dijo en la reunión.

examples.en_text: That team always beats us by cheating, which is why we have it in for them in today's game.
examples.target_text: Ese equipo siempre nos gana con trampa, por eso le tenemos ganas en el partido de hoy.

examples.en_text: The tax inspectors have had it in for that company for a long time.
examples.target_text: Los inspectores de hacienda le tienen ganas a esa empresa desde hace tiempo.

examples.en_text: I know you have it in for Carlos because he took your position, but you must be professional.
examples.target_text: Sé que le tienes ganas a Carlos porque te quitó el puesto, pero debes ser profesional.

explanation_en: This pronominal verb phrase is the standard way to say 'to reach an agreement' or 'to agree' among multiple parties. It is much more common in spoken Spanish than the verb 'acordar' when referring to people coming to a mutual understanding.

examples.en_text: My parents could never agree on where to go on vacation.
examples.target_text: Mis padres nunca se ponían de acuerdo sobre a dónde ir de vacaciones.

examples.en_text: The designers couldn't agree on the color of the new logo.
examples.target_text: Los diseñadores no se ponían de acuerdo con el color del nuevo logotipo.

examples.en_text: Every time we went out, they would quickly agree on what to eat.
examples.target_text: Cada vez que salíamos, ellos se ponían de acuerdo muy rápido sobre qué comer.

examples.en_text: My roommates could never agree on cleaning the kitchen.
examples.target_text: Mis compañeros de piso nunca se ponían de acuerdo para limpiar la cocina.

examples.en_text: Although they argued a lot, the two directors always reached an agreement in the end.
examples.target_text: Aunque discutían mucho, los dos directores siempre se ponían de acuerdo al final.

examples.en_text: Why did you guys never agree when you worked together?
examples.target_text: ¿Por qué ustedes nunca se ponían de acuerdo cuando trabajaban juntos?
